records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֥ת אַהֲרֹ֖ן וּמֹשֶׁ֑ה בְּי֗וֹם דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּהַ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of Aaron and Moses on [the] day spoke Yahweh with Moses on [the] mount of Sinai.
pieces: This is the family line of Aaron and Moses at the time when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

L.1: And these [are] the generations of Aaron and Moses on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

R.1: This is the family of Aaron and Moses at the time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

decisions.choice: generations: the family line that comes from someone
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to give birth" and heads family records through Genesis (Genesis 2:4; 5:1; 11:27). Here only Aaron's sons follow (verses 2-4). Moses is named because he and Aaron head the tribe of Levi together, but his own sons are counted among the ordinary Levites (1 Chronicles 23:13-14), so the record goes on with the priestly line.

decisions.choice: on the day: at the time when
decisions.reason: "On the day" often means "when" or "at the time" rather than one day of twenty-four hours (Genesis 2:4). It places these men at the time of the laws given at Sinai.

decisions.choice: family line / family
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the list is; "generations" in this sense is no longer common English. Literal keeps the old term so the reader can link it to the other family records.

records.heading: The family line of Aaron and Moses

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה שְׁמ֥וֹת בְּֽנֵי־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַבְּכ֣וֹר׀נָדָ֑ב וַאֲבִיה֕וּא אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] names of [the] sons of Aaron: the firstborn Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
pieces: These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

L.2: And these [are] the names of the sons of Aaron: the firstborn Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

R.2: Aaron's sons were Nadab, who was the oldest, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

decisions.choice: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar: the four sons of Aaron
decisions.reason: The same four are named in Exodus 6:23 and 28:1, where they are chosen with their father to serve as priests.

records.source: אֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים הַמְּשֻׁחִ֑ים אֲשֶׁר־מִלֵּ֥א יָדָ֖ם לְכַהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: These [are the] names of [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, the anointed, whom he filled their hand to serve as priest.
pieces: These were the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests.

L.3: These [are] the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whose hand he filled to serve as priests.

R.3: They were the priests. They had been anointed with oil and set apart to serve as priests.

decisions.choice: filled their hand: ordained, installed in the office
decisions.reason: "To fill the hand" is the Hebrew way of saying that someone is installed as priest (Exodus 28:41; 29:9; Judges 17:5). The picture may come from placing the parts of the ordination offering in the priests' hands (Leviticus 8:27).

decisions.choice: he filled: Moses, acting at God's command
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. In Leviticus 8 it is Moses who carries out the ordination, as the LORD commanded him (Exodus 29:1-9; Leviticus 8:33).

decisions.choice: the anointed priests: priests set apart by anointing with oil
decisions.reason: Oil was poured or sprinkled on Aaron and his sons to set them apart as holy for God's service (Exodus 30:30; Leviticus 8:12, 30).

decisions.choice: who were ordained
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the passive because the Hebrew does not name who ordained them (m2) and "filled their hand" would not be understood (m1). Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: וַיָּ֣מָת נָדָ֣ב וַאֲבִיה֣וּא לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֡ה בְּֽהַקְרִבָם֩ אֵ֨שׁ זָרָ֜ה לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר סִינַ֔י וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־הָי֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וַיְכַהֵ֤ן אֶלְעָזָר֙ וְאִ֣יתָמָ֔ר עַל־פְּנֵ֖י אַהֲרֹ֥ן אֲבִיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And died Nadab and Abihu before Yahweh when they brought near strange fire before Yahweh in [the] wilderness of Sinai, and sons not were to them; and served as priest Eleazar and Ithamar on [the] face of Aaron their father.
pieces: But Nadab and Abihu died in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when they offered an improper fire before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the lifetime of their father Aaron.

L.4: And Nadab and Abihu died before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when they brought near strange fire before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons; and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests before the face of Aaron their father.

R.4: But Nadab and Abihu died in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That happened in the Sinai desert, when they offered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the wrong kind of fire. They had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was still alive.

decisions.choice: strange fire: the fire of Leviticus 10:1-2
decisions.reason: The verse recalls how Nadab and Abihu offered fire that the LORD had not commanded and were consumed by fire from before him (Leviticus 10:1-2; Numbers 26:61). "Strange" means not authorized, outside what God had laid down; the exact fault is not explained.

decisions.choice: they had no sons: no priestly line came from them
decisions.reason: The priesthood passed from father to son. Because the two died without sons, the priesthood continued only through Eleazar and Ithamar (1 Chronicles 24:1-2).

decisions.choice: on the face of Aaron their father: in Aaron's presence, during his lifetime
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in the sight of" or "during the life of" (Genesis 11:28). Eleazar and Ithamar served while Aaron was still alive and high priest, under his eye.

decisions.choice: That happened in the Sinai desert ...
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long sentence and states the place and the cause in separate sentences.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the opening of a speech of the LORD
decisions.reason: This formula opens each of the LORD's instructions in the chapter (verses 11, 14, 44). Verses 6-10 give the Levites' place under the priests.

records.heading: The Levites given to Aaron

records.source: הַקְרֵב֙ אֶת־מַטֵּ֣ה לֵוִ֔י וְֽהַעֲמַדְתָּ֣ אֹת֔וֹ לִפְנֵ֖י אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְשֵׁרְת֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Bring near [the] tribe of Levi, and make stand it before Aaron the priest, and they will serve him.
pieces: "Bring the tribe of Levi forward and present them to Aaron the priest to assist him.

L.6: "Bring the tribe of Levi near, and make it stand before Aaron the priest, and they shall serve him.

R.6: "Bring the tribe of Levi to Aaron the priest. They are to help him.

decisions.choice: bring near: bring forward for service
decisions.reason: The verb is used for presenting someone or something before God or a priest (8:9-10; Exodus 29:4). Here it marks the Levites out for a new task.

decisions.choice: serve him: assist Aaron as his helpers
decisions.reason: The verb means to minister or to wait on someone, as Joshua served Moses (Exodus 24:13; 33:11). The Levites are not priests; they help the priests (18:2-7).

decisions.choice: the tribe of Levi: the tribe Aaron and Moses came from
decisions.reason: Levi is the tribe left out of the military census of chapter 1 (1:47-53). It is now given its own work and its own count.

records.source: וְשָׁמְר֣וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתּ֗וֹ וְאֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֨רֶת֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֥ת הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And they will keep his charge and [the] charge of all the congregation before [the] tent of meeting, to serve [the] service of the tabernacle.
pieces: They are to carry out duties for him and for the whole congregation in front of the tent of meeting as they do the work of the tabernacle.

L.7: And they shall keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, to do the service of the tabernacle.

R.7: They will do work for him and for the whole community at the meeting tent. They will take care of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: keep his charge: carry out the duties given to them, on his behalf
decisions.reason: The noun means a watch, a duty, something entrusted to someone's care. The Levites guard and serve for Aaron, and for the whole people, who could not themselves come near the holy things (1:53; 18:3-4).

decisions.choice: the service of the tabernacle: its work, especially carrying and caring for it
decisions.reason: "Service" here is labor: taking the tabernacle down, carrying it and setting it up (1:50-51; 4:1-33), not the offerings, which belong to the priests.

decisions.choice: carry out duties / do work
decisions.reason: "Keep the charge" is a set phrase in these chapters. Balanced and Readable say what it means; Literal keeps "charge" each time.

records.source: וְשָׁמְר֗וּ אֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵי֙ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְאֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֥ת הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And they will keep all [the] articles of [the] tent of meeting, and [the] charge of [the] sons of Israel, to serve [the] service of the tabernacle.
pieces: They are to take care of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and carry out the duties of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} as they do the work of the tabernacle.

L.8: And they shall keep all the articles of the tent of meeting and the charge of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to do the service of the tabernacle.

R.8: They will take care of everything used in the meeting tent. They will do the work at the tabernacle for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: articles: the furnishings and equipment of the tent
decisions.reason: The word covers any object made for a purpose: vessels, tools and furniture. The items given to each clan are listed in verses 25-26, 31 and 36-37.

decisions.choice: the charge of the sons of Israel: the duty owed by all Israel, done in their place
decisions.reason: The Levites do for the whole people what the people themselves owe to the sanctuary, as in verse 7.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּה֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְאַהֲרֹ֖ן וּלְבָנָ֑יו נְתוּנִ֨ם נְתוּנִ֥ם הֵ֨מָּה֙ ל֔וֹ מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And you will give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons; given, given [are] they to him from [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. From among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} they are given entirely to him.

L.9: And you shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons; they [are] given, given to him from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.9: Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given to him from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to belong to him completely.

decisions.choice: given, given: wholly given
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a word to make it stronger. The Levites are handed over completely to Aaron, as a gift from the people (8:16, 19; 18:6).

decisions.choice: to him: to Aaron
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "to him", that is, to Aaron. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation read "to me", as in 8:16, where the LORD says the Levites are given to him. Both are true in the book: the Levites belong to the LORD (verse 12) and are given to Aaron for service. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: given entirely / to belong to him completely
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the force of the repeated word (m1) with "entirely" and "completely". Literal keeps the repetition.

records.source: וְאֶת־אַהֲרֹ֤ן וְאֶת־בָּנָיו֙ תִּפְקֹ֔ד וְשָׁמְר֖וּ אֶת־כְּהֻנָּתָ֑ם וְהַזָּ֥ר הַקָּרֵ֖ב יוּמָֽת׃פ
records.gloss: And Aaron and his sons you will appoint, and they will keep their priesthood; and the stranger who comes near will be put to death.
pieces: Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out their duties as priests. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death."

L.10: And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood; and the outsider who comes near shall be put to death."

R.10: Put Aaron and his sons in charge, to do the work of priests. Anyone else who comes near the holy things must be put to death."

decisions.choice: appoint: put in charge of an office
decisions.reason: The verb used for counting the people in this chapter (verse 15) also means to put someone in charge (1:50; Genesis 39:4-5). Here it means to appoint.

decisions.choice: the outsider: anyone who is not a priest
decisions.reason: The word means a stranger or someone not belonging. In matters of the sanctuary it means anyone outside the priestly family, even a Levite or another Israelite (17:5; 18:7). It does not mean a foreigner here.

decisions.choice: who comes near: who approaches to do the priests' work
decisions.reason: "Come near" is used for drawing close to the altar and the holy things to serve (18:3, 7). The danger is in taking the priests' place, not in coming to the sanctuary to worship.

decisions.choice: comes near the holy things
decisions.reason: Readable says what is approached, following m3, so the reader does not think every visitor to the tent was killed.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a new speech: why the Levites belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Verses 12-13 give the reason for the Levites' special place.

records.heading: The Levites in place of the firstborn

records.source: וַאֲנִ֞י הִנֵּ֧ה לָקַ֣חְתִּי אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם מִתּוֹךְ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל תַּ֧חַת כָּל־בְּכ֛וֹר פֶּ֥טֶר רֶ֖חֶם מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And I, look, I have taken the Levites from among [the] sons of Israel instead of every firstborn, [the] opening of [the] womb from [the] sons of Israel; and will be to me the Levites.
pieces: "Look, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} have taken the Levites from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in place of every firstborn, the first child born to each mother in Israel. The Levites belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.12: "And I, look, I have taken the Levites from among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in place of every firstborn that opens the womb among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and the Levites shall be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

R.12: "I have chosen the Levites from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They will take the place of every oldest son in Israel, the first baby each mother has. The Levites belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: opening of the womb: the first child a mother bears
decisions.reason: The phrase defines "firstborn" by the mother: her first child (Exodus 13:2, 12). The firstborn sons of Israel were claimed by God (verse 13).

decisions.choice: in place of: the Levites stand in for Israel's firstborn
decisions.reason: Instead of each family giving its firstborn son to serve the LORD, the tribe of Levi is given to him in their place (verses 40-51; 8:16-18).

decisions.choice: And I, look: an emphatic opening
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" stands first, before the word that calls for attention. It stresses that this is God's own act.

decisions.choice: every oldest son
decisions.reason: Readable says "oldest son" because verses 40-43 show that the firstborn males are meant, and "firstborn" is a hard word for young readers.

records.source: כִּ֣י לִי֮ כָּל־בְּכוֹר֒ בְּיוֹם֩ הַכֹּתִ֨י כָל־בְּכ֜וֹר בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם הִקְדַּ֨שְׁתִּי לִ֤י כָל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵאָדָ֖ם עַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה לִ֥י יִהְי֖וּ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For to me [is] every firstborn; on [the] day I struck every firstborn in [the] land of Egypt I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, from man to beast. To me they will be. I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: For every firstborn is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. When I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I made holy to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They are to be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.13: For every firstborn [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} every firstborn in Israel, from {{gender:human|man}} to beast. They shall be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.13: Every firstborn belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When I killed all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} every firstborn in Israel, both people and animals. They belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: the day I struck every firstborn in Egypt: the last plague
decisions.reason: God struck the firstborn of Egypt and passed over Israel's houses (Exodus 12:12, 29). From then on Israel's firstborn, of people and of animals, belonged to him (Exodus 13:2, 11-15).

decisions.choice: I set apart: made holy, claimed as belonging to God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something holy, set apart for God's own use. The firstborn were his; that is why they had to be given to him or bought back (Exodus 13:13; 34:20).

decisions.choice: from man to beast: people and animals alike
decisions.reason: A way of saying "all", from one end of the range to the other. The Levites replace the firstborn sons; firstborn animals of the Levites replace those of Israel's livestock (verses 41, 45).

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh: the seal on the command
decisions.reason: The closing words give God's own name as the authority for what he has said, as often in Leviticus (Leviticus 18:5; 19:12).

decisions.choice: made holy to myself
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "made holy" to keep the link with "holy" (m2); Literal and Readable use "set apart".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינַ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses in [the] wilderness of Sinai, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. He said,

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,

R.14: In the Sinai desert, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sinai: the dry country around the mountain
decisions.reason: Israel was still camped near Mount Sinai (1:1). "Wilderness" is open, dry grazing land, not necessarily sand desert.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: Readable uses the more familiar word "desert" for the wilderness, as in verse 4.

records.heading: A census of the Levites

records.source: פְּקֹד֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י לֵוִ֔י לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָ֖ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם כָּל־זָכָ֛ר מִבֶּן־חֹ֥דֶשׁ וָמַ֖עְלָה תִּפְקְדֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Enroll [the] sons of Levi by [the] house of their fathers, by their clans; every male from a son of a month and upward you will enroll them.
pieces: "Enroll the Levites by their ancestral families and their clans. Enroll every male one month old and up."

L.15: "Enroll the sons of Levi by the house of their fathers, by their clans; every male from a son of a month and upward you shall enroll them."

R.15: "Count the Levites by their families and clans. Count every boy and man who is at least one month old."

decisions.choice: enroll: count and record by name
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit, inspect or muster, and in the census lists to count and register people (1:2-3, 19). The same verb means "appoint" in verse 10.

decisions.choice: every male from one month old: a count for the sanctuary, not for war
decisions.reason: The other tribes were counted from twenty years old as men able to go to war (1:3). The Levites are counted from one month, the age at which a firstborn son was bought back (18:15-16), because they are to stand in place of Israel's firstborn (verses 40-43).

decisions.choice: house of their fathers, clans: the family groups within a tribe
decisions.reason: A tribe was made up of clans, and a clan of ancestral households, each named for a forefather (1:2).

decisions.choice: enroll / count
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use "enroll", as in the census of chapter 1, and Readable "count", each time the verb is used for the census in this chapter.

records.source: וַיִּפְקֹ֥ד אֹתָ֛ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צֻוָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And enrolled them Moses according to [the] mouth of Yahweh, as he had been commanded.
pieces: So Moses enrolled them at the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as he had been commanded.

L.16: And Moses enrolled them at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as he had been commanded.

R.16: So Moses counted them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him to do.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of Yahweh: at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says. Moses acts on the LORD's spoken word (verses 39, 51; 9:18).

decisions.choice: just as the LORD had told him
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who commanded, whom the Hebrew passive leaves unnamed but plain from the context.

records.source: וַיִּֽהְיוּ־אֵ֥לֶּה בְנֵֽי־לֵוִ֖י בִּשְׁמֹתָ֑ם גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן וּקְהָ֖ת וּמְרָרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And were these [the] sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.
pieces: These were the names of Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

L.17: And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.

R.17: Levi had three sons: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

decisions.choice: Gershon, Kohath and Merari: the sons of Levi
decisions.reason: The same three are listed in Genesis 46:11 and Exodus 6:16. Each gives his name to one of the three Levite groups whose work and camp are set out in verses 21-37.

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה שְׁמ֥וֹת בְּֽנֵי־גֵרְשׁ֖וֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם לִבְנִ֖י וְשִׁמְעִֽי׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] names of [the] sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
pieces: The names of the sons of Gershon, by their clans, were Libni and Shimei.

L.18: And these [are] the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.

R.18: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei. Each of them was the head of a clan.

decisions.choice: by their clans: each son is the head of a clan
decisions.reason: The phrase means the names are given as clan names. Each son's descendants form a clan (verse 21; Exodus 6:17).

decisions.choice: Each of them was the head of a clan.
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what "by their clans" means (m1).

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י קְהָ֖ת לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם עַמְרָ֣ם וְיִצְהָ֔ר חֶבְר֖וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵֽל׃

pieces: The sons of Kohath, by their clans, were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

L.19: And the sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

R.19: Kohath's sons, the heads of his clans, were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

decisions.choice: Amram: the father of Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Amram's clan is the family of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6:18, 20), so the priests come from the Kohathites.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֧י מְרָרִ֛י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֑י אֵ֥לֶּה הֵ֛ם מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הַלֵּוִ֖י לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָֽם׃

pieces: The sons of Merari, by their clans, were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites by their ancestral families.

L.20: And the sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These [are] the clans of the Levites by the house of their fathers.

R.20: Merari's sons, the heads of his clans, were Mahli and Mushi. Those were the clans of the Levites, family by family.

decisions.choice: these are they: a closing summary of the list
decisions.reason: The words close the list of clans begun in verse 17. Each group is now taken in turn, with its count, its camp, its leader and its work (verses 21-37).

records.source: לְגֵ֣רְשׁ֔וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת֙ הַלִּבְנִ֔י וּמִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַשִּׁמְעִ֑י אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֔ם מִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּֽי׃
records.gloss: To Gershon [belonged the] clan of the Libnite[s] and [the] clan of the Shimeite[s]; these [are] they, [the] clans of the Gershonite[s].
pieces: From Gershon came the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These were the Gershonite clans.

L.21: To Gershon [belonged] the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these [are] the clans of the Gershonites.

R.21: The Libnite clan and the Shimeite clan came from Gershon. They were the Gershonite clans.

decisions.choice: to Gershon: the clans descended from Gershon
decisions.reason: "To Gershon" marks what belongs to him, here the clans that come from his two sons (verse 18). The same form opens the Kohathite and Merarite sections (verses 27, 33).

records.source: פְּקֻדֵיהֶם֙ בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר כָּל־זָכָ֔ר מִבֶּן־חֹ֖דֶשׁ וָמָ֑עְלָה פְּקֻ֣דֵיהֶ֔ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת אֲלָפִ֖ים וַחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Their enrolled [men], by [the] number of every male from a son of a month and upward, their enrolled [men were] seven thousand and five hundred.
pieces: The number of those enrolled, counting every male one month old and up, was 7,500.

L.22: Their enrolled [men], by the number of every male from a son of a month and upward, their enrolled [men were] 7,500.

R.22: When they counted every boy and man at least one month old, there were 7,500.

decisions.choice: their enrolled, their enrolled: the subject said twice
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the subject, adds how the count was made, and names it again before the total. It is the pattern of the census lists (1:20-21).

decisions.choice: thousand: a numeral, the same word as in the census of chapter 1
decisions.reason: On the size of the numbers and the other meaning the word can have, see the note at 1:21.

records.source: מִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֑י אַחֲרֵ֧י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן יַחֲנ֖וּ יָֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: [The] clans of the Gershonite[s] behind the tabernacle will camp, westward.
pieces: The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west side.

L.23: The clans of the Gershonites shall camp behind the tabernacle, westward.

R.23: The Gershonite clans were to set up their tents behind the tabernacle, on the west side.

decisions.choice: behind the tabernacle, westward: the back of the tent was its west side
decisions.reason: The tabernacle faced east, toward the sunrise (verse 38; Exodus 27:13), so "behind" is west. The word for west is literally "seaward", toward the Mediterranean Sea.

decisions.choice: camp: an inner ring of Levites round the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The three Levite groups camp on three sides of the tabernacle and the priests on the fourth, between the sanctuary and the other tribes (1:53; 2:17).

decisions.choice: were to camp
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is future in form, giving the arrangement as an order. Balanced and Readable use "were to", which fits the report of the census.

records.source: וּנְשִׂ֥יא בֵֽית־אָ֖ב לַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֑י אֶלְיָסָ֖ף בֶּן־לָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] leader of [the] house of [the] father for the Gershonite[s was] Eliasaph son of Lael.
pieces: The leader of the ancestral family of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.

L.24: And the leader of the father's house of the Gershonites [was] Eliasaph son of Lael.

R.24: The leader of the Gershonite families was Eliasaph son of Lael.

decisions.choice: leader of the father's house: the chief of the whole Gershonite group
decisions.reason: Here "father's house" is used of the whole group descended from Gershon, and its leader is over all its clans (compare verses 30, 35).

records.source: וּמִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת בְּנֵֽי־גֵרְשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן וְהָאֹ֑הֶל מִכְסֵ֕הוּ וּמָסַ֕ךְ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And [the] charge of [the] sons of Gershon in [the] tent of meeting [was] the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and [the] screen of [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting,
pieces: In the tent of meeting, the Gershonites were in charge of the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

L.25: And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting [was] the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and the screen of the entrance of the tent of meeting,

R.25: At the meeting tent, the Gershonites took care of the cloth parts of the tabernacle. These were the inside curtains, the tent over them, its covers, and the curtain at the entrance of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle and the tent: the inner curtains and the tent of goats' hair over them
decisions.reason: In the building instructions, "the tabernacle" is the set of fine woven curtains and "the tent" is the cover of goats' hair spread over it (Exodus 26:1, 7). The Gershonites carry the fabric parts (4:24-26).

decisions.choice: its covering: the skins laid over the tent
decisions.reason: Ram skins dyed red and a further covering of fine leather lay on top of the tent (Exodus 26:14).

decisions.choice: the screen of the entrance: the curtain across the doorway of the tent
decisions.reason: A woven hanging closed the east entrance of the tent (Exodus 26:36). It is different from the veil before the ark.

decisions.choice: the cloth parts of the tabernacle ... inside curtains
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two technical terms of m1 so the list makes sense to a reader who does not know Exodus 26.

records.source: וְקַלְעֵ֣י הֶֽחָצֵ֗ר וְאֶת־מָסַךְ֙ פֶּ֣תַח הֶֽחָצֵ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֧ר עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן וְעַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִ֑יב וְאֵת֙ מֵֽיתָרָ֔יו לְכֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and [the] hangings of the courtyard, and [the] screen of [the] entrance of the courtyard which [is] around the tabernacle and around the altar, and its cords, for all its service.
pieces: the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its cords. They did all the work connected with these things.

L.26: and the hangings of the courtyard, and the screen of the entrance of the courtyard, which [is] around the tabernacle and the altar, and its cords, for all its service.

R.26: They also took care of the curtains around the courtyard, the curtain at the courtyard gate, and the ropes. The courtyard went around the tabernacle and the altar. The Gershonites did all the work needed for these things.

decisions.choice: the hangings of the courtyard: the linen walls of the outer court
decisions.reason: The court around the tabernacle was fenced by linen hangings on posts (Exodus 27:9-18). The posts themselves are the Merarites' load (verse 37).

decisions.choice: which is around the tabernacle and the altar: the courtyard surrounds both
decisions.reason: The clause describes the courtyard, whose hangings enclosed the tabernacle and the altar of burnt offering in front of it.

decisions.choice: its cords, for all its service: the ropes, and all the work these things require
decisions.reason: "Its" refers back to the things listed, taken together. The Gershonites carry them, put them up and take them down (4:26).

decisions.choice: They did all the work connected with these things.
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "for all its service" into a sentence, which closes the list that began in verse 25. Literal keeps the bare phrase.

records.source: וְלִקְהָ֗ת מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַֽעַמְרָמִי֙ וּמִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַיִּצְהָרִ֔י וּמִשְׁפַּ֨חַת֙ הַֽחֶבְרֹנִ֔י וּמִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָֽעָזִּיאֵלִ֑י אֵ֥לֶּה הֵ֖ם מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הַקְּהָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And to Kohath [belonged the] clan of the Amramite[s], and [the] clan of the Izharite[s], and [the] clan of the Hebronite[s], and [the] clan of the Uzzielite[s]; these [are] they, [the] clans of the Kohathite[s].
pieces: From Kohath came the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These were the Kohathite clans.

L.27: And to Kohath [belonged] the clan of the Amramites, and the clan of the Izharites, and the clan of the Hebronites, and the clan of the Uzzielites; these [are] the clans of the Kohathites.

R.27: The Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite and Uzzielite clans came from Kohath. They were the Kohathite clans.

decisions.choice: to Kohath: the clans descended from Kohath
decisions.reason: As in verse 21. The four clans are named for the four sons of verse 19.

records.source: בְּמִסְפַּר֙ כָּל־זָכָ֔ר מִבֶּן־חֹ֖דֶשׁ וָמָ֑עְלָה שְׁמֹנַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: By [the] number of every male from a son of a month and upward, eight thousand and six hundred, keepers of [the] charge of the holy place.
pieces: Counting every male one month old and up, there were 8,600. They were responsible for the care of the holy place.

L.28: By the number of every male from a son of a month and upward, [there were] 8,600, keeping the charge of the holy place.

R.28: When they counted every boy and man at least one month old, there were 8,600. They took care of the holy things.

decisions.choice: 8,600: the number in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The three Levite totals, 7,500, 8,600 and 6,200 (verses 22, 28, 34), add up to 22,300, but verse 39 gives the whole as 22,000. One suggested explanation is a copying slip in this verse: in Hebrew "six" (shesh) and "three" (shalosh) differ by one letter, and some manuscripts of the Greek translation read 8,300 here, which would make the three groups add up to exactly 22,000. Others take 22,000 in verse 39 as a round figure. The Hebrew text is followed here; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: keepers of the charge of the holy place: those who guard and care for the holy things
decisions.reason: "The holy place" here means the sanctuary and its most holy furniture, which the Kohathites were to carry (verse 31; 4:4-15).

decisions.choice: by the number: the census formula, without "their enrolled"
decisions.reason: This verse leaves out the words "their enrolled" that frame verse 22, but the sense is the same.

records.source: מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת בְּנֵי־קְהָ֖ת יַחֲנ֑וּ עַ֛ל יֶ֥רֶךְ הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן תֵּימָֽנָה׃
records.gloss: [The] clans of [the] sons of Kohath will camp on [the] side of the tabernacle, southward.
pieces: The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.

L.29: The clans of the sons of Kohath shall camp on the side of the tabernacle, southward.

R.29: The Kohathite clans were to set up their tents on the south side of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: the side, southward: to the right of one facing east
decisions.reason: The word for south also means "right hand" (Genesis 13:9), seen from someone facing the sunrise, as the tabernacle did. The tribe of Reuben camped on the south beyond them (2:10), and Korah the Kohathite later joined Reubenites in revolt (16:1).

decisions.choice: were to camp
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

records.source: וּנְשִׂ֥יא בֵֽית־אָ֖ב לְמִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת הַקְּהָתִ֑י אֶלִיצָפָ֖ןבֶּן־עֻזִּיאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] leader of [the] house of [the] father of [the] clans of the Kohathite[s was] Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
pieces: The leader of the ancestral family of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

L.30: And the leader of the father's house of the clans of the Kohathites [was] Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

R.30: The leader of the Kohathite families was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

decisions.choice: Elizaphan son of Uzziel: a cousin of Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Uzziel was a brother of Amram (verse 19; Exodus 6:18, 22). Elizaphan, also called Elzaphan, helped carry away the bodies of Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10:4).

records.source: וּמִשְׁמַרְתָּ֗ם הָאָרֹ֤ן וְהַשֻּׁלְחָן֙ וְהַמְּנֹרָ֣ה וְהַֽמִּזְבְּחֹ֔ת וּכְלֵ֣י הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְשָׁרְת֖וּ בָּהֶ֑ם וְהַ֨מָּסָ֔ךְ וְכֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And their charge [was] the ark, and the table, and the lampstand, and the altars, and [the] articles of the holy place with which they will serve, and the screen, and all its service.
pieces: They were in charge of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the holy utensils used in the priests' ministry, the screen, and all the work connected with these things.

L.31: And their charge [was] the ark, and the table, and the lampstand, and the altars, and the articles of the holy place with which they minister, and the screen, and all its service.

R.31: They took care of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the holy things used in worship. They also cared for the curtain in front of the ark. They did all the work needed for these things.

decisions.choice: the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars: the most holy furniture
decisions.reason: The ark of the testimony stood in the most holy place; the table for the bread of the presence, the lampstand and the gold altar of incense stood in the holy place, and the bronze altar of burnt offering in the courtyard (Exodus 25-27; 30:1-6). The Kohathites carried them once the priests had covered them (4:4-15).

decisions.choice: with which they minister: the vessels used in the sanctuary service
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of priests serving at the altar (Exodus 28:43). "They" refers to those who serve in the sanctuary, chiefly the priests; the Kohathites carry the vessels but do not use them in worship (4:15).

decisions.choice: the screen: here the veil before the ark
alternatives: the screen at the entrance of the tent
decisions.reason: Among the most holy things "the screen" is most likely the veil hung in front of the ark, called "the veil of the screen" in 4:5, which covered the ark on the march. The Gershonites carried the other screens (verses 25-26).

decisions.choice: used in the priests' ministry
decisions.reason: Balanced names the priests as those who use the vessels (m2).

decisions.choice: the curtain in front of the ark
decisions.reason: Readable says which screen is meant, following m3.

records.source: וּנְשִׂיא֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הַלֵּוִ֔י אֶלְעָזָ֖ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֑ן פְּקֻדַּ֕ת שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And [the] leader of [the] leaders of the Levite[s was] Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; [the] oversight of [the] keepers of [the] charge of the holy place.
pieces: The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He oversaw those responsible for the care of the holy place.

L.32: And the leader of the leaders of the Levites [was] Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, [with] oversight of those keeping the charge of the holy place.

R.32: Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, was the chief over all the leaders of the Levites. He was in charge of the men who took care of the holy things.

decisions.choice: leader of the leaders: the chief leader
decisions.reason: Hebrew forms a superlative by joining a noun to its own plural, as in "holy of holies". Eleazar is over the three leaders named in verses 24, 30 and 35.

decisions.choice: the priest: Aaron, or Eleazar himself
decisions.reason: The words "the priest" can belong to Aaron, as usual in these chapters (verse 6), or to Eleazar, who is also a priest (4:16). The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: oversight: supervision of the work
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb translated "enroll" and "appoint" (verses 10, 15). Eleazar oversees the Kohathites in particular, and Ithamar the other two groups (4:16, 28, 33).

L.33: To Merari [belonged] the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites; these [are] the clans of Merari.

R.33: The Mahlite clan and the Mushite clan came from Merari. They were the Merarite clans.

decisions.choice: to Merari: the clans descended from Merari
decisions.reason: As in verses 21 and 27. The clans are named for the two sons of verse 20.

L.34: And their enrolled [men], by the number of every male from a son of a month and upward, [were] 6,200.

R.34: When they counted every boy and man at least one month old, there were 6,200.

decisions.choice: their enrolled: the census formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 22. On the total of the three groups, see the note at verse 28.

pieces: The leader of the ancestral family of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.

L.35: And the leader of the father's house of the clans of Merari [was] Zuriel son of Abihail; they shall camp on the side of the tabernacle, northward.

R.35: The leader of the Merarite families was Zuriel son of Abihail. The Merarites were to set up their tents on the north side of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: northward: the last side, with the east kept for the priests
decisions.reason: With the Gershonites west (verse 23), the Kohathites south (verse 29) and the Merarites north, the east side, facing the entrance, is left for Moses, Aaron and his sons (verse 38).

decisions.choice: were to camp
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

pieces: The Merarites were appointed to take charge of the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, posts and bases, all its equipment and all the work connected with them,

L.36: And the oversight of the charge of the sons of Merari [was] the frames of the tabernacle, and its bars, and its pillars, and its bases, and all its articles, and all its service,

R.36: The Merarites were given the job of taking care of the wooden frames of the tabernacle. They took care of its crossbars, posts and bases, and all the tools for them. They did all the work needed for these things.

decisions.choice: frames, bars, pillars, bases: the wooden framework of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The tabernacle stood on upright frames of acacia wood set in silver bases and held together by crossbars; posts held the veil and the entrance screen (Exodus 26:15-32, 37). These heavy parts were carried on wagons (7:8).

decisions.choice: the oversight of the charge: the duty assigned to them
decisions.reason: The two nouns together mean the task given into their care (verse 32; 4:32).

decisions.choice: frames: upright wooden panels or open frames
decisions.reason: The word was once often understood as solid boards. It may describe open frames, which would be lighter to carry; either way they formed the walls of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:15-25).

decisions.choice: wooden frames
decisions.reason: Readable adds "wooden" from Exodus 26:15, so the reader can picture the frames.

L.37: and the pillars of the courtyard all around, and their bases, and their pegs, and their cords.

R.37: They also took care of the posts that stood around the courtyard, with their bases, tent pegs and ropes.

decisions.choice: the pillars of the courtyard, pegs and cords: the frame of the outer fence
decisions.reason: The courtyard hangings hung from posts standing in bronze bases, held up with pegs and ropes (Exodus 27:10-19; 35:18). The Gershonites carried the hangings, the Merarites the posts (verse 26).

decisions.choice: posts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "posts" because "pillars" suggests stone columns; Literal keeps the usual word.

records.source: וְהַחֹנִ֣ים לִפְנֵ֣י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֡ן קֵ֣דְמָה לִפְנֵי֩ אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֨ד׀מִזְרָ֜חָה מֹשֶׁ֣ה׀וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן וּבָנָ֗יו שֹֽׁמְרִים֙ מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַמִּקְדָּ֔שׁ לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהַזָּ֥ר הַקָּרֵ֖ב יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And those camping before the tabernacle eastward, before [the] tent of meeting toward sunrise, [were] Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping [the] charge of the sanctuary for [the] charge of [the] sons of Israel; and the stranger who comes near will be put to death.
pieces: Those who were to camp in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses, Aaron and his sons. They were to carry out the duties of the sanctuary on behalf of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.

L.38: And those camping before the tabernacle eastward, before the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, [were] Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.

R.38: Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons were to set up their tents on the east side, in front of the meeting tent, facing the sunrise. They were to take care of the holy tent for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Anyone else who came near the holy things had to be put to death.

decisions.choice: eastward, toward the sunrise: in front of the entrance
decisions.reason: The entrance of the tabernacle faced east (Exodus 27:13-16). Those camped there guarded the way in. Judah's camp lay beyond them on the same side (2:3).

decisions.choice: for the charge of the sons of Israel: on Israel's behalf
decisions.reason: The priests' care of the sanctuary is a duty done for the whole people, as the Levites' work is in verses 7-8.

decisions.choice: the outsider who comes near: anyone not authorized
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, an outsider is anyone who is not a priest who tries to do the priests' work or enter the holy places.

decisions.choice: the sanctuary: the holy place
decisions.reason: The word is built from the root "holy", and means God's holy dwelling, the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8).

decisions.choice: came near the holy things
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts the words "and Aaron" have dots written over them, a scribal mark that may show doubt about them. The LORD's command in verse 15 and the report in verse 16 name Moses alone, and the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Syriac translation do not have "and Aaron". The words are kept here, as in the Hebrew text. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: 22,000: less than the sum of the three groups
decisions.reason: Verses 22, 28 and 34 add up to 22,300. See the note at verse 28. The figure of 22,000 is the one used for the exchange with Israel's firstborn in verses 43-46.

decisions.choice: every firstborn male from one month old: the sons the LORD claimed
decisions.reason: These are the firstborn sons whom the Levites replace (verses 12-13). One month is the age at which a firstborn son was to be bought back (18:16), which is why the Levites too were counted from that age (verse 15).

decisions.choice: take the number of their names: count them name by name
decisions.reason: The phrase "take the head" or "take the number" means to count, and "by names" means each person was recorded individually (1:2, 18).

decisions.choice: oldest son
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh: set in the middle of the command
decisions.reason: The words break into the sentence to give the command God's authority. The Levites are taken for him, not for Moses or Aaron.

decisions.choice: the livestock of the Levites in place of the firstborn livestock
decisions.reason: Firstborn animals belonged to the LORD and were offered or bought back (Exodus 13:12-13). Here the Levites' animals as a whole are taken in exchange for the firstborn of Israel's flocks and herds at that time. Later firstborn animals were still given to the priests (18:15-18).

decisions.choice: (I [am] the LORD)
decisions.reason: Literal shows with parentheses and Balanced with dashes that the words break into the sentence (m1); Readable moves them to a sentence of their own.

R.42: So Moses counted all the oldest sons of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him to.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh had commanded him: obedience to the word
decisions.reason: The phrase recurs through the chapter (verses 16, 51) and marks each step as done exactly as God said.

decisions.choice: So Moses enrolled every firstborn ..., as the LORD had commanded him.
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the object next to the verb; Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which places the command first.

records.gloss: And was every firstborn male by [the] number of names, from a son of a month and upward, by their enrolled [men], two and twenty thousand three and seventy and two hundred.
pieces: The total of firstborn males one month old and up, enrolled by name, was 22,273.

L.43: And every firstborn male, by the number of names from a son of a month and upward, by their enrolled [men], was 22,273.

R.43: There were 22,273 oldest sons at least one month old, counted by name.

decisions.choice: 22,273: a small number of firstborn for so large a people
decisions.reason: Set beside 603,550 men of fighting age (1:46), 22,273 firstborn sons would mean very large families. Some explain the figure as the firstborn born since the LORD claimed them at the exodus (Exodus 13:2); others relate it to the meaning of "thousand" discussed at 1:21. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: by their enrolled: as they were counted
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the census formula: this is the total of those registered.

decisions.choice: a new speech: the exchange is carried out
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Verses 45-48 tell how the firstborn are exchanged for the Levites and what is done with those left over.

pieces: "Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Levites shall be mine: the exchange made final
decisions.reason: The command of verse 41 is now carried out, and the Levites belong to the LORD as the firstborn did (verses 12-13; 8:14).

decisions.choice: their livestock: the livestock of the Israelites
decisions.reason: "Their" refers back to the Israelites, whose firstborn animals are replaced (verse 41).

decisions.choice: the Israelites' animals
decisions.reason: Readable names whose animals are meant (m2).

records.source: וְאֵת֙ פְּדוּיֵ֣י הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְהַשִּׁבְעִ֖ים וְהַמָּאתָ֑יִם הָעֹֽדְפִים֙ עַל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִבְּכ֖וֹר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

L.46: And [as] the redemption of the 273 of the firstborn of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who are in excess over the Levites,

R.46: There are 273 more oldest sons among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} than there are Levites. They must be bought back.

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to buy back a firstborn
decisions.reason: The word is from the verb "to redeem", to set free by payment. A firstborn son belonged to the LORD and had to be bought back (Exodus 13:13-15; 34:20). Each Levite set one firstborn free; the 273 with no Levite to replace them were bought back with money.

decisions.choice: the 273: the difference between the two counts
decisions.reason: The firstborn number 22,273 (verse 43) and the Levites 22,000 (verse 39), leaving 273.

decisions.choice: There are 273 more ... They must be bought back.
decisions.reason: Readable states the difference as two sentences, where Literal and Balanced keep the sentence running into verse 47.

R.47: For each of them collect {{units:about 2 ounces of silver, weighed by the official weight used at the holy tent|five shekels, weighed by the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs}}.

decisions.choice: five, five shekels: five shekels each
decisions.reason: Saying a number twice means "so many each". "Per head" (literally "per skull") means for each person.

decisions.choice: five shekels by the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight of silver, about 11.5 grams. The sanctuary shekel was the official standard, fixed at twenty gerahs (Exodus 30:13; Leviticus 27:25). Five shekels is the price of redeeming a firstborn son (18:16) and the valuation of a boy from one month to five years (Leviticus 27:6).

decisions.choice: about 2 ounces of silver, by the sanctuary standard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the shekels and gerahs as the Measures setting; Literal keeps the units. Five shekels is about 2 ounces.

decisions.reason: The word means silver, the metal used for payment, and so "money".

decisions.choice: to Aaron and his sons: what belongs to the LORD goes to his priests
decisions.reason: The redemption price belongs to the LORD, and he gives it to the priests (18:8, 15-16).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף הַפִּדְי֑וֹם מֵאֵת֙ הָעֹ֣דְפִ֔ים עַ֖ל פְּדוּיֵ֥י הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.source: מֵאֵ֗ת בְּכ֛וֹר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לָקַ֣ח אֶת־הַכָּ֑סֶף חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְשִׁשִּׁ֜ים וּשְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת וָאֶ֖לֶף בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: From [the] firstborn of [the] sons of Israel he took the money: five and sixty and three hundred and a thousand, by [the] shekel of the holy place.
pieces: From the firstborn of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} he collected {{units:about 34 pounds of silver by the sanctuary standard|1,365 shekels by the sanctuary shekel}}.

L.50: From the firstborn of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel he took the money: 1,365 [shekels] by the shekel of the sanctuary.

R.50: He collected {{units:about 34 pounds of silver, weighed by the official weight|1,365 shekels, weighed by the sanctuary shekel}} for the oldest sons of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: 1,365: five shekels for each of the 273
decisions.reason: 273 times five shekels makes 1,365 shekels (verses 46-47). The Hebrew gives the number from the smallest part up: five and sixty and three hundred and a thousand.

decisions.choice: about 34 pounds of silver
decisions.reason: 1,365 shekels at about two-fifths of an ounce each is about 34 pounds. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight with the shekels as the Measures setting; Literal keeps the shekels and supplies the unit the Hebrew leaves understood.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־כֶּ֧סֶף הַפְּדֻיִ֛ם לְאַהֲרֹ֥ן וּלְבָנָ֖יו עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And gave Moses [the] money of the ransoms to Aaron and to his sons according to [the] mouth of Yahweh, as had commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.51: And Moses gave the money of the redemption to Aaron and to his sons at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.51: Moses gave the money to Aaron and his sons, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. He did just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of Yahweh, as Yahweh commanded: the chapter's closing note of obedience
decisions.reason: The two phrases together stress that Moses did exactly what he was told, as in verses 16 and 42.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had said. He did just what ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the two phrases into two sentences so that neither is lost.
